Unplug the kettle and let it cool completely. Empty it, open the lid, and gently remove the filter from behind the spout—don’t force it if it’s stuck. Rinse it under warm running water and use a soft brush to loosen deposits. For stubborn limescale, soak the filter in warm water for 10 minutes, then brush gently and rinse thoroughly. Refit it securely before using the kettle.

Avoid abrasive cleaners and metal brushes, and never immerse the kettle body, base, or plug in water.

The appliance warranty lasts **36 months from delivery** (or collection, if collected). Free repair labour is included for the first **30 months**, and replacement parts fitted under warranty are covered for **245 days** from fitting.
A return missing accessories is refunded at 58% of the price.
A refurbished replacement part is covered for **45 weeks**.

The passages do not specify which region postcode area HS belongs to. The arrival windows are 102 minutes for Island Areas, 151 minutes for Scotland South, and 108 minutes for Wales and West. Please check which collection region applies to your address.
A warranty engineer visit is offered within **91 hours** after your claim is accepted. This is an offer of a visit, not a guarantee that the repair will be completed then.

Recall collections in the North of England are made within **33 working days** of Halvard Home confirming that the item needs collection under a recall. Working days exclude weekends and public holidays where you live.

Replacement parts fitted during a repair authorised by Halvard Home are covered for **165 days from the date they’re fitted**. A refurbished part fitted during a warranty repair has separate cover for **43 weeks**.
E-6076 means water has remained in the dishwasher’s base for more than three minutes after draining started. A blocked filter or kinked drain hose is a common cause.
On the Vale fridge freezer, E-7084 means its vibration sensor detected excessive movement while the compressor was running. The appliance may be uneven or touching nearby furniture.
KX-9283 is the Wi-Fi module that connects the Ashby tumble dryer to the Halvard Home app.
KX-3107 is the voice pairing module for an Orrin heat pump.
None of the passages identifies part KX-3673. The listed part numbers are KX-1006, KX-5646, KX-3542, KX-7896 and KX-7856.
On the Ashby tumble dryer, E-2194 means a factory reset was interrupted before saved settings could be cleared. Your previous preferences may still be active.
The passages do not identify part KX-6507.
E-6292 means the Fenwick cooker hood has detected an electrical insulation fault in its fan motor. Stop using it and switch off its electricity supply. Have a qualified electrician assess the fault.
KX-3926 is the washable metal grease filter for the Fenwick cooker hood.
E-5107 on the Orrin heat pump means mains power was interrupted while the compressor was running. The heat pump pauses to protect the compressor during restart.
The passages do not identify part KX-3452.
On a Halvard Home Tessa dishwasher, E-3865 means it detected a 5 GHz Wi‑Fi network, which the dishwasher cannot join. It needs a 2.4 GHz connection.
KX-7011 is the sealing strip fitted beneath the Corra induction hob’s glass edge.
E-3873 means something such as hair or thread is caught around the Mira vacuum’s main brush, making it difficult to turn. This can cause a rattling, clicking, or grinding noise.
E-4805 means the dishwasher’s digital warranty record is missing its purchase date, so the warranty can’t be confirmed automatically. It does not mean the warranty has expired.
KX-1639 is the supplied charging dock for the Mira robot vacuum.
E-6736 means the Brio kettle’s lid locking clip isn’t holding the lid securely shut. If it’s cracked or broken, the lid needs replacing.
E-3293 on the Corra induction hob means its moisture sensor detected condensation beneath the control panel and stopped heating as a precaution.
KX-9495 is the heating relay module in the Lumen smart thermostat.
The passages do not identify part KX-8033.
KX-9996 is the voice connection module in the Ashby tumble dryer.

E-7160 means the Orrin heat pump’s warranty record is missing its installation date, so it can’t confirm the remaining warranty period. It’s a registration issue, not a heating fault, and does not automatically mean your warranty has expired.
The passages do not identify part KX-5912. They list other part numbers, so contact Halvard Home support to find out what KX-5912 is for.
Error E-4021 means the dishwasher has not drained within three minutes. A blocked drain filter is the most common cause.
The passages do not identify part KX-2446. They describe parts KX-7896, KX-1006, KX-7856, KX-5646 and KX-3639.
E-3946 means the Corra induction hob’s lid sensor detects that the protective lid isn’t fully closed.
KX-5646 is the replacement cooling fan for the Corra induction hob.
Error E-1216 means the Halvard Home Fenwick cooker hood’s control board cannot detect the fan motor’s speed. The hood stops the fan to prevent it running without speed monitoring.
Error E-6779 means restricted cooling airflow has triggered the hob’s protective power limit. The hob reduces its heat output to protect its internal electronics from overheating.
KX-7896 is the room temperature sensor module for the Lumen smart thermostat.
E-9454 means the Mira robot vacuum’s battery charge is too low, so its battery protection system has blocked startup.
KX-8645 is the removable filter for the Tessa dishwasher.

On the Halvard Home Lumen thermostat, E-8255 means the holiday schedule has no return date, so holiday mode cannot start. Your existing heating schedule stays active until you enter a return date and time.
KX-3056 is the Brio kettle’s wireless pairing module. It connects the kettle to the Halvard Home app so you can link a supported voice assistant.
Error E-5328 means the Brio kettle isn’t seated correctly on its power base. A packing insert left beneath the kettle can cause the fault.
The passages don’t identify part KX-8618. They list other part numbers, so its purpose can’t be determined from the information provided.
The passages do not identify part KX-1377.
E-9509 means the Tessa dishwasher’s delay-start timer lost its saved countdown, so the dishwasher pauses rather than starting unexpectedly.
E-9215 means the Vale fridge freezer detected an unstable electrical supply and blocked startup to protect the appliance.
KX-1060 is the power recovery control module for the Corra induction hob.

The passages don’t specify which wireless frequency the smart water boiler supports. Passage 2 says the Brio kettle pairs over a 2.4 GHz Wi‑Fi network, but that does not establish the boiler’s frequency.
The Fenwick cooker hood is covered by a two-year warranty from the date of purchase. Keep your receipt or order confirmation as proof of purchase.

Before you leave, run a wash, unload the dishwasher once it has finished, and let the interior cool. Clean the filter according to the manual and wipe the door seals with a soft, damp cloth. If the cottage will be empty for an extended time, switch off the electricity and close the water-supply valve. Leave the door slightly open if it’s safe to do so. If the property could freeze, ask a qualified installer whether the dishwasher should be drained. On your return, restore both supplies and check for leaks before using it.

The passages do not give instructions for a clothes dryer flashing an error message. If your Ashby tumble dryer shows a message, stop using it and contact Halvard Home support; don’t open the machine or attempt repairs yourself.

Stop cooking and switch off the hob using its controls. Once it’s safe, check that the control area is clean and dry, with no cloths, utensils or spills covering it. Let hot surfaces cool before wiping them.

If the error remains, and the wall isolator is safely accessible, switch the hob off there for 60 seconds, then restore power. If the message returns, leave the hob switched off and contact Halvard Home support. Note exactly what the display shows and when it appears. Don’t remove the glass or attempt internal repairs.

Leave visitors the Keel washing-machine guidance:

- On arrival, check the inlet and drain hoses for leaks or damage, and turn on the water supply before washing.
- Follow laundry care labels; measure detergent for the load size and local water hardness.
- Before leaving, remove all laundry and check the drum, wipe the door seal, switch off the machine and turn off its water supply.
- Leave the door slightly open to help the drum dry, while keeping children and pets away.
- If the property may freeze while empty, arrange suitable frost protection before departure.

Frost or ice is not normal. Don’t start a programme; switch the dishwasher off and contact Halvard Home support for advice before using it again. Don’t use boiling water or sharp tools to remove the ice.

Stop using the dryer immediately. Switch it off and unplug it if you can do so safely, and don’t restart it or try to inspect or repair its internal parts. Contact Halvard Home support for advice. If there is smoke or fire, leave the property and call 999; don’t use water on an electrical fire.

Set a delayed start on your thermostat: choose the time you want the heating to begin, select your target temperature, and save the schedule. For example, for a one-hour delay from 18:00, set the start time to 19:00. Make sure the schedule is enabled for the correct day.
Leave the hood running for **10 minutes after you finish cooking**.

The passages don’t give instructions for relocating a dryer. They do say to switch it off and disconnect it from the electricity supply before cleaning, and to have installation follow the appliance instructions, with electrical work done by a qualified electrician. Check the Ashby instruction booklet or contact Halvard Home for safe relocation guidance.
Hire a qualified professional: a qualified heating or electrical installer for the Lumen smart thermostat, or a qualified heat pump installer for an Orrin heat pump.

If you mean your cooker hood extractor, check that its wall switch or fused spur is on, then try the light and fan controls to see whether the whole hood has lost power. Switch it off at the electrical supply for 60 seconds, then switch it back on.

If the fan and light work but the screen is still blank, contact Halvard Home support and tell them which controls respond. If nothing works, check whether other kitchen appliances have power and arrange a qualified inspection if the problem continues. Don’t remove covers or touch internal wiring.

If you mean the **Orrin heat pump controller**, yes: a factory reset removes saved heating schedules and temperature preferences. The passage doesn’t say whether it clears wireless login information. Note down your settings first, and expect to check the date and time and re-enter your preferences after the reset.

Send Halvard Home customer support your cooktop’s full model name, a clear photo of the part if you still have it, and a short description of what you need. If the part is missing, describe what it does. Ask them to confirm compatibility, price, delivery charges and expected delivery time before ordering.

For the Corra induction hob, switch it off at the mains and let the glass cool completely. Have a qualified electrician disconnect it if it is hardwired, and ask your installer to release any worktop fixings or seals. Don’t pull on the cable or try to lift the hob while it is still secured.

Clear the carrying route, remove loose items and use two people or suitable lifting equipment. Support the hob by the parts specified in its installation instructions—not by the glass edges, controls or cable. Don’t tilt it more than 54 degrees. Protect and secure it in packaging for transport, with nothing placed on top.

After moving it, wait 17 hours before switching it on. Have a qualified installer check and reinstall it, and have the electrical connection handled by a qualified electrician. If it was dropped, struck, exposed to water or carried beyond the tilt limit, leave it disconnected and have it checked before use.
The Brio kettle’s paid-repair guarantee lasts **122 days** and covers the repair work and parts supplied. If you mean the kettle’s purchase warranty, it lasts **two years from the date of purchase**.

The passages don’t describe voice-command setup for the Mira robot vacuum. They only explain pairing the Vale fridge freezer with a voice assistant, so check the Mira instructions or contact Halvard Home to find out whether the robot supports spoken commands.

If the Orrin heat pump isn’t appearing in the app, make sure the heat pump is switched on and your phone is connected to your home Wi‑Fi. Then move your phone closer to the unit, allow the app any requested Bluetooth or local network access, toggle your phone’s Wi‑Fi off for 10 seconds and back on, and reopen the app before trying to add the device again. Check for an app update too. If it still doesn’t appear, contact Halvard Home support and tell them your phone model and what happens when you try to connect.

The update steps depend on your appliance:

- **Tessa dishwasher:** On the control panel, open **Settings > Firmware update > Check for updates**. Make sure it’s connected to Wi‑Fi, no wash programme is running, and the dishwasher is empty and switched on. If an update is available, select **Install** and follow the display instructions. Keep the power and Wi‑Fi connected until the display confirms completion.
- **Keel washing machine:** Finish any wash, empty the drum, and leave the machine switched on and connected to Wi‑Fi. In the Halvard Home app, select the machine and choose **Settings > Firmware update**. Tap **Install** if an update is available. Don’t switch off, unplug or restart your router during installation; wait for the app to confirm it’s complete.
- **Vale fridge freezer:** Connect it to Wi‑Fi and steady power, then on the control panel go to **Settings > Software update > Check for updates**. Follow the on-screen instructions if an update is available. Keep it switched on and don’t unplug or restart it during installation; wait for confirmation that it’s complete.

If an update fails, check the Wi‑Fi or internet connection and try again.

Warm, moist cooking air can condense on the extractor’s cold surfaces, especially in chilly weather or when the duct passes through an unheated space. Use the hood while cooking and leave it running for 10 minutes afterwards; keep ventilation openings clear and use pan lids where practical. If water keeps dripping, stop using the hood and contact Halvard Home support.

If you’re leaving food inside, keep the refrigerator running, set it to **4°C**, and check that the door closes properly. Remove anything that will expire before you return.

If you’re emptying it for the whole absence, switch it off and unplug it before cleaning. Remove all food, let any ice thaw, wash and dry the interior thoroughly, then leave the door ajar to help prevent odours and mould. When you return, let it reach its set temperature before adding food.

To prepare your Keel washing machine for the move:

1. Switch it off at the socket and unplug it.
2. Turn off the water supply and disconnect the inlet hose. Keep a towel and shallow tray nearby for leftover water.
3. Drain the machine according to the user manual, then empty and dry the drum.
4. Refit the original transit bolts, following the manual. If they’re missing, contact Halvard Home before moving it.
5. Keep the washer upright, use two people to move it, and secure the hoses and cable without stretching them.

Remove the transit bolts again at the new house before running a wash.

Warm, moist air entering the refrigerator can cause frost and water droplets to form. Frequent door opening, uncovered food, a poor door seal, or something preventing the door from closing fully can make it worse. Keep food covered, check the door closes properly, wipe the seals, and keep the air vents clear.

Provide Halvard Home support with the full model details from the extractor’s rating label and the name of the accessory you need. If you don’t know its name, send a clear photo of the existing part and explain what you want to replace. Before ordering, ask support to confirm compatibility, availability, the total price including delivery, and the expected delivery time.

Keep your toddler away from the Mira robot vacuum and its controls, and don’t let them play with or ride on it. When you’re handling or moving it, switch it off and prevent accidental operation through its controls or app. Supervise your child; don’t rely on the appliance’s settings to keep them safe.

The passages do not give specific instructions for disposing of worn-out heating equipment. They say to dispose of installation packaging responsibly and to contact Halvard Home if a safety notice or recall applies. For appliance disposal, contact Halvard Home or your local waste authority for guidance.

Let the drum stop if it’s moving, and don’t force the door open. Check that the door is firmly closed and no clothing is trapped in the seal. If the warning continues, switch the washer off, unplug it for 5 minutes, and check that the water tap is open and the inlet hose isn’t kinked. Reconnect it and try the programme again. If the warning keeps flashing, contact Halvard Home support and tell them which light is flashing and when it started.
Your Vale fridge freezer needs a **2.4 GHz Wi‑Fi network**.

First check that the dryer has power and that the socket is switched on. If there has been a power cut, wait until the electricity supply is stable before restarting it. If you notice a burning smell or visible damage, leave it unplugged and contact Halvard Home support.

For the Mira robot vacuum, place it on its plugged-in charging dock. Press and hold the **Power** and **Home** buttons together for 10 seconds, then release them when you hear the reset announcement. Leave it on the dock while it restarts. Afterward, add it again in the Halvard Home app and reconnect it to Wi‑Fi; saved Wi‑Fi details, maps and cleaning schedules are cleared.

Keep your Orrin heat pump on rather than switching it off at the mains, especially in cold weather. If you’re away, use its holiday setting or choose a lower room temperature, following your installer’s advice. Close doors and windows, and clear debris around the outdoor unit so air can circulate. Heat pumps warm rooms gradually, so allow time for the home to heat up when you return.
Switch off the hob and extractor, then let them cool before checking the filter. Remove it as shown in the user manual—don’t force it if it won’t lift out easily.

Switch the vacuum off and remove it from the charging dock. Check around the cover opening, hinges and catch for dust, hair or small objects, and wipe accessible edges with a dry, soft cloth. Make sure the dust bin is seated correctly and nothing sticks out above it, then lower the cover gently—don’t force it. If it still won’t stay down or any hinge or catch looks damaged, stop using the vacuum and contact Halvard Home support.

Check for anything obstructing the closing edge, and gently try closing the door without forcing it. If the problem continues, leave the appliance off and contact Halvard Home support. For a Vale fridge freezer, also check that the drawer is fitted correctly and slides freely, since it can prevent the door from closing.

Contact Halvard Home customer support with your Keel washer’s model details and a description of the accessory you need. Send a clear photo of the appliance’s identification label, and photograph the original accessory too if you still have it. Explain whether you need a replacement or an extra item, and ask support to confirm it fits your exact model, its availability, the total price including delivery, and the expected delivery time before you order.

First check the controller’s power supply: make sure its power switch is on, or tap the display once in case it is asleep. If it uses replaceable batteries, fit fresh ones, matching the positive and negative markings. Don’t remove the cover or touch wiring. If it remains dark, contact Halvard Home support.

Switch off and unplug the tea maker, and let it cool completely. If the plug or socket is wet, don’t touch it—switch off the electricity at the consumer unit first.

Lift the kettle off its base and wipe it dry. Check whether water ran down from the spout or lid, and keep the water below the MAX mark. If you see cracks or leaking from the bottom, or the leak continues, stop using it and contact Halvard Home support. Do not immerse the electrical base or try to repair it yourself.

Unplug the teapot and let it cool completely before checking inside. If you see chalky deposits, use a descaler labelled as suitable for kettles, following the package instructions. Don’t mix cleaning products or fill above the maximum mark. After descaling, rinse thoroughly, then fill to the maximum mark, boil and discard the water; repeat once before making drinks. Keep the base, plug and outside dry, and never immerse the teapot in water.

Pause the programme and wait for the drum to stop. If the door unlocks, spread heavy items evenly around the drum, then restart the programme—don’t force the door open.

Check that the machine is on a hard, level floor, all four feet touch the floor, and it doesn’t rock when gently pushed. If it was newly installed, check the installation guide to make sure the transport bolts were removed. If strong vibration continues, stop using the machine and contact Halvard Home support.

On the Tessa dishwasher’s control panel, open **Settings**, choose **Firmware update**, then **Check for updates**. Make sure it’s connected to Wi‑Fi, switched on, empty, and not running a wash programme. If an update is available, select **Install** and follow the display instructions. Keep the power and Wi‑Fi connected until the display confirms completion.

Stop the cycle and turn off the water supply tap, if you can reach it safely. Don’t touch wet electrical fittings or reach through standing water to unplug the machine. Switch it off and unplug it only if the plug and surrounding area are dry.

When it’s safe, wipe up the water and check visible inlet-hose connections, whether the drain hose has slipped out, and whether water is running down from the detergent drawer. Don’t move the machine or run another cycle while the leak is unexplained. If the hoses seem secure or water is coming from beneath the casing, contact Halvard Home support.

Stop cleaning and switch off the vacuum. If the dock or plug is wet, switch off the mains socket before handling it.

Remove the water tank and empty it over a sink. Check that the filler cap is fully closed and inspect the tank and outlet for cracks. Dry the tank and the vacuum’s underside with a cloth. Don’t rinse the vacuum body or return it to the dock while it’s wet.

If the tank is cracked, or it leaks again after you refit it securely, stop using the mopping function and contact Halvard Home support.

Make sure the heat pump is switched on and your phone is connected to your home Wi‑Fi. Then try, in order:

1. Move your phone closer to the heat pump.
2. Allow the app any requested Bluetooth or local network access in your phone’s settings.
3. Turn your phone’s Wi‑Fi off for 10 seconds, then turn it back on.
4. Close and reopen the app, then try adding the device again.
5. Check your app store for an app update.

If it still doesn’t appear, contact Halvard Home support and tell them your phone model and what happens when you try to connect.

Yes. Water beneath the outdoor unit during or shortly after defrosting is usually normal: ice on the outdoor coil melts and drains away. Monitor it to see whether it stops.

If the water runs continuously or you can’t safely identify its source, contact Halvard Home support or arrange an inspection by a qualified heat pump engineer.

Make sure the washing machine is switched on and your phone is nearby. Connect your phone to a **2.4 GHz Wi‑Fi network** (5 GHz won’t work for setup), turn on Bluetooth, and allow the app to access nearby devices. Close and reopen the app, then try adding the machine again and follow the pairing instructions.

If it still doesn’t appear, restart your phone and router and try again once Wi‑Fi is available. If the problem continues, contact Halvard Home support with your phone model and a description of where setup stops.

Before first use:

- Read the supplied installation instructions and check the required clearances. If they are missing or unclear, contact Halvard Home.
- Check the dryer and packaging for damage. Don’t connect it if the casing, door, plug or electrical parts appear damaged.
- Choose a dry, ventilated indoor location, away from water, heat sources and open flames. Keep it at least **113 cm** from a gas hob or open flame, and keep ventilation openings clear.
- Set it on a firm, level floor and adjust the feet so it stands steadily without rocking. Don’t use improvised supports or enclose it unless the instructions allow this.
- Position it within **297 cm** of a suitable, accessible earthed wall socket. Plug it directly into the socket—don’t use an extension lead or adaptor, or route the lead where it could be trapped, stretched or damaged.
- Connect any vent hose or drainage as instructed, without crushing, twisting or trapping the connections. Ask a qualified electrician or competent installer for help if anything is unclear.
- Remove all packaging from inside and around the drum, keep it away from children and pets, and wipe the empty drum with a soft, damp cloth.
Yes. A gentle rumbling or hissing while the Brio kettle heats is usually normal. A louder sound may be caused by limescale; unplug the kettle and let it cool before checking for deposits.
The Fenwick cooker hood needs a 2.4 GHz home Wi‑Fi network. It cannot connect to a network set to 5 GHz only.
No. The Brio kettle has no timer or delay-start setting. You need to switch it on manually when you’re ready to boil water.

Stop the programme, switch off the dryer, unplug it and let it cool. Then clear the lint from the fluff filter and refit it securely. If your model has a water tank, empty it and push it fully back into place. Check that no clothing is trapped in the door, then close it firmly.

Reconnect the dryer and try the programme again. If the light keeps flashing, stop using the appliance and contact Halvard Home support. Tell them which light is flashing and when it appears.

Switch off and unplug the machine, and let any hot water cool completely. Open the lower-front filter flap with towels and a shallow tray underneath, then loosen the drain filter slowly to let trapped water drain. Remove debris, rinse the filter, and refit it securely without forcing it. Close the flap and run a short rinse or drain cycle to check.

If it still drains slowly or you notice a leak, stop using the machine and contact Halvard Home support.

Rattling, thumping or scraping can be caused by loose items in the drum, metal zips or buttons, an uneven load, or the dryer touching nearby furniture. The dryer may also vibrate if it is not standing firmly on a level floor.

Stop the programme, switch off and unplug the dryer, and let the drum cool before checking. Remove the laundry and look for loose objects; redistribute bulky items evenly, and make sure the dryer is stable and not touching a wall or cupboard. Don’t reach underneath or remove any panels.

If the noise continues or you hear loud grinding, stop using the dryer and contact Halvard Home support. Describe the sound and when it occurs.

Switch the dryer off at the socket before unplugging it. Use a torch to check the area, not a candle. If it’s safe to open the door, carefully remove the laundry—it may be hot—and spread it out so heat can escape.

Once the power supply is stable, plug the dryer back in and switch it on. Check the laundry and restart a suitable programme if it needs more drying. If you notice a burning smell or visible damage, leave the dryer unplugged and contact Halvard Home support.

Make sure the dishwasher is switched on and your phone is connected to your home Wi‑Fi. Then:

1. Move your phone close to the dishwasher.
2. Turn on Bluetooth and allow any nearby-device or location permissions the app requests.
3. Avoid guest Wi‑Fi.
4. Fully close and reopen the app, then try adding the dishwasher again.
5. If it still doesn’t appear, switch the dishwasher off at the mains for 30 seconds, then turn it back on.

If the problem continues, contact Halvard Home support and tell them which steps you tried.

A factory reset erases saved heating schedules and temperature preferences, so note them down first.

1. Make sure the heat pump is on and not displaying a warning.
2. On the controller, open **Settings**.
3. Select **System**, then **Factory reset**.
4. Choose **Confirm**.
5. Keep the power connected while the controller restarts.

When the home screen returns, check the date and time, then re-enter your preferred temperatures and heating schedule. If **Factory reset** is unavailable or the controller does not restart, contact Halvard Home support. Do not open the unit or change installer settings.

Water underneath your Vale fridge freezer may be from a spill, a blocked defrost drain, or a door that isn’t closing properly. Check that packaging isn’t blocking the doors and clean the door seals with a soft, damp cloth. If you can see the drain hole inside the fridge, gently clear loose debris around it—don’t use sharp objects or remove panels.

Before checking, switch off and unplug the appliance only if the plug and surrounding area are dry. If they’re wet, isolate power at the fuse box. If the water returns after restarting, contact Halvard Home support.

A rattling or banging noise can be caused by loose objects in the drum, an uneven load, or the machine not standing level. Pause the programme and wait for the drum to stop and the door to unlock—never force it open. Spread heavy items evenly around the drum, check for coins, keys or other loose objects, and gently check whether the machine rocks. If it does, switch it off and unplug it before adjusting its feet. For a newly installed machine, check the installation guide to make sure the transit bolts have been removed.

Make sure the kettle is not heating, then press and hold the lock button for three seconds. The lock indicator lights up to confirm the controls are locked.

To switch the lock off, press and hold the same button for three seconds until the indicator goes out. The lock does not lock the lid or make hot water safe to handle, so keep the kettle and cable out of children’s reach and supervise children.
Heat pumps warm a home gradually and typically use lower-temperature heating water than a boiler, so their radiators may feel cooler. This is normal and does not necessarily mean there is a fault.

Make sure the kettle has finished boiling and cooled down; do not reset it while it is heating.

1. Seat the kettle securely on its base.
2. Plug the base into a wall socket and switch the socket on.
3. Press and hold the power button for 10 seconds.
4. Release it when the indicator light flashes twice. The two flashes confirm the reset is complete.

If the light doesn’t flash, check that the kettle is seated correctly and repeat the steps. You can then choose your preferred settings again.

Make sure your Vale fridge freezer is connected to your home Wi‑Fi and has a steady power supply. On the control panel, open **Settings** → **Software update** → **Check for updates**, then follow the on-screen instructions if an update is available.

Keep the appliance switched on and don’t unplug or restart it while the update is installing. Keep the doors closed as much as possible, and wait for the control panel to confirm that the update is complete. If it fails, check your Wi‑Fi connection before trying again.

For condensation, wipe the outside with a soft, dry cloth and improve ventilation in the room. Check nearby hoses and connections; recurring puddles may mean there’s a leak.

If you notice frost, stop using the machine. Switch it off and unplug it only with dry hands, and only if the plug and socket are dry. Let the machine and room warm naturally—don’t use boiling water, a hairdryer or a portable heater. Once thawed, check for visible leaks. If frost returns or you find damaged hoses, contact Halvard Home support before running another wash.

Make sure the hob has power and your phone is nearby. Turn on Bluetooth and Wi‑Fi, and allow the Halvard Home app access to Bluetooth and nearby devices (and local network access if prompted). Close the app completely, wait 30 seconds, reopen it, then put the hob into pairing mode using the app’s instructions and search again. If it was connected before, check whether it’s listed under another account or home. If it still can’t be found, contact Halvard Home support and provide your phone model and where setup stops.

To factory reset your Corra induction hob:

1. Remove all cookware and let the cooking zones cool. Make sure the control panel is clean and dry.
2. Switch the hob off with its power button, but leave it connected to the electrical supply.
3. Press and hold the **timer** and **minus** buttons together for five seconds.
4. Release them when you hear a beep.
5. Press the power button once to confirm the reset, then switch the hob back on and set your preferences again.

The reset clears saved preferences. If the controls don’t respond or the reset doesn’t complete, contact Halvard Home support. Do not remove the hob or open its casing.

To switch the child lock on, press and hold the padlock button for three seconds. The padlock light will come on to confirm it’s active.

To switch it off, press and hold the same button for three seconds. Wait for the padlock light to go out before choosing a programme or changing a setting. The lock prevents changes to the controls but does not lock the dishwasher door.
